name: Jotham
bio:
Jotham was Gideon's youngest son. When his brother Abimelech hired reckless men and killed all seventy of Gideon's sons on a single stone, Jotham alone escaped by hiding (Judges 9:5).

After the men of Shechem made Abimelech king, Jotham stood on top of Mount Gerizim and told them a famous fable: the trees asked the olive, the fig, and the vine to be king over them in turn, and each refused, asking why they should give up their own goodness to rule over others; finally the trees asked the thornbush, which answered that if the trees truly meant to anoint it king in good faith, they should take shelter in its shade — but if not, let fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon (Judges 9:7-15). Jotham used the fable to point out that the thornbush offered no real shade yet arrogantly claimed kingship, just as Abimelech, with none of Gideon's accomplishments, had seized the throne; he sharply rebuked the Shechemites for forgetting how Gideon had risked his life for them, choosing instead to crown the murderer of Gideon's own sons (Judges 9:16-20). He then pronounced a curse — that if the Shechemites had not dealt faithfully and honestly with Abimelech, let fire consume them both — and fled to Beer out of fear of his brother (Judges 9:20-21).

Three years later, the Shechemites and Abimelech did indeed turn on each other in betrayal and mutual destruction, and Scripture specifically notes that this was the fulfillment of Jotham's curse (Judges 9:56-57), making his fable one of the most literary and ultimately fully vindicated prophecies in the book of Judges.
